title: IBM’s AI-powered vulnerability clearinghouse finds hundreds of Java flaws
key_facts: IBM's Lightwell clearinghouse has found and fixed more than 400 vulnerabilities in popular Java libraries, announced Tuesday 6 Oct 2026
Lightwell is now generally available; customers can request priority security reviews of specific open-source flaws
Linux Foundation's Akrites and Chainguard's Athena are similar clearinghouses
Datadog said in February that nearly six in 10 Java services contain at least one exploitable vulnerability
IBM stresses backporting fixes into live apps so customers need not choose between security and uptime
quote_evidence: IBM’s vulnerability discovery clearinghouse has found and fixed more than 400 vulnerabilities in popular Java libraries, the company announced on Tuesday.
Finding those bugs is only half the battle: the real work is backporting fixes directly into active production apps so customers do not have to pick between security and uptime
why_it_matters_hint: AI-assisted patching for widely used open-source Java code.
